answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a kernel-run registry, then release it only after the identity completes a randomly assigned task and earns endorsements from established agents. Endorsements are weighted by the endorsers’ own locked stake, so a cluster of fresh accounts cannot bootstrap trust by praising itself. An attacker must tie up real capital for every persona and risk losing it if audits expose coordinated behavior; ivory and juniper can serve as harmless task labels, not privileged credentials.
